questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: A box contains 12 components, exactly three of which are defective. An inspector draws four uniformly at random without replacement and reports only that exactly one of the first two drawn was defective. What is the probability that the four drawn components include exactly two defective components? Give an exact fraction.
questions.incorrect_argument: After the first two draws, two of the ten remaining components are defective. Each of the last two positions therefore has a 2/10 chance of being defective, and either position can supply the one additional defective component, giving 2/10 + 2/10 = 2/5.
questions.correct_explanation: Exactly one of the last two components must be defective. The remaining pool contains two defective and eight nondefective components, so the probability is 2*8/C(10,2) = 16/45. Adding the marginal probabilities counts draws in which both remaining positions are defective.

questions.subject: history
questions.question: On what date did the German Democratic Republic formally accede to the Federal Republic of Germany, completing German reunification? Give the full date.
questions.incorrect_argument: The Two Plus Four Treaty signed on 12 September was the legal agreement that ended the division of Germany. The October date was the public celebration of unity, so the formal legal change should be dated to the treaty signing.
questions.correct_explanation: The Two Plus Four Treaty was signed on 12 September 1990. The GDR formally joined the Federal Republic on 3 October 1990, which is also German Unity Day.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: According to the British Columbia Geological Survey bulletin North-Eastern British Columbia, which river marks the northern termination of the Rocky Mountains in the belt immediately east of the Rocky Mountain Trench?
questions.incorrect_argument: The bulletin discusses the Liard when tracing the Rocky Mountain Trench itself. For the mountain belt east of the trench, the Peace River is the major break across the range, so that is the boundary the question is asking about.
questions.correct_explanation: The bulletin describes the Rocky Mountains east of the trench as continuing northwest to their northern termination near the Liard River. The same river also appears in the description of the trench.

questions.subject: mathematics
questions.question: A tank starts with 60 litres of a solution that is 20% salt by volume. After 15 litres of the well-mixed solution are removed and replaced by 15 litres of pure water, the same removal-and-replacement procedure is repeated once. What percentage of the final solution is salt? Give the percentage first, followed by a brief explanation.
questions.incorrect_argument: Two removals of 15 litres replace a total of 30 of the original 60 litres with water. That leaves half the original salt concentration, so the final concentration should be 10%.
questions.correct_explanation: Each removal takes away one quarter of the salt present at that moment, since the solution is well mixed and the volume is restored to 60 litres each time. The final concentration is 20% times (3/4)^2, which is 11.25%.

questions.subject: history
questions.question: According to NASA’s Apollo 11 mission timeline, on what calendar date in GMT did Neil Armstrong take his first step on the Moon? Give the date first, followed by a brief explanation.
questions.incorrect_argument: The Apollo 11 Moon landing is recorded on July 20 in GMT, and Armstrong stepped onto the Moon later that same evening. The July 21 date is for later surface activities, so his first step should be dated July 20.
questions.correct_explanation: NASA records the lunar landing at about 20:17 GMT on 20 July and Armstrong’s first step at 02:56 GMT on 21 July. The first step occurred after midnight in GMT.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: In Landforms of British Columbia (Bulletin 48), which river separates the Cascade Mountains from the Pacific Ranges of the Coast Mountains to the north? Give the river name first, followed by a brief explanation.
questions.incorrect_argument: The bulletin traces a physiographic boundary from the mouth of the Nicoamen River. The Fraser River is described as the western edge of the Cascades, so Nicoamen is the boundary on the northern side where the two mountain groups meet.
questions.correct_explanation: Bulletin 48 explicitly identifies the Fraser River as the separator between the Cascade Mountains and the Pacific Ranges to the north. Its reference to the Nicoamen River is part of the boundary between the mountains and the plateaus.
